title: Keep organics out of landfills
summary: California requires local organics recycling programs and recovery of edible food from specified businesses. Solana Center helps jurisdictions and businesses with education, inspections, records, and technical support.
who: CalRecycle oversees implementation. Local jurisdictions run and enforce programs. Residents and businesses follow local collection rules; designated food businesses have food recovery duties.
solanaRole: Solana Center documents SB 1383 education, business assistance, food recovery inspections, capacity planning, and reporting support for local jurisdictions.

milestones.label: Law enacted
milestones.detail: Governor Brown signed SB 1383, Chapter 395, Statutes of 2016.

milestones.label: Implementation requirements begin
milestones.detail: The organics regulations took effect. Jurisdictions began required programs and education.

milestones.label: Local enforcement begins
milestones.detail: Jurisdictions had to begin enforcement by this date, with notice and time to correct violations before continuing violations receive penalties.

milestones.label: Statewide organics target
milestones.detail: Target: 75% less organic waste disposal than in 2014. This is a statutory target, not a claim that it was met.

milestones.label: Statewide food recovery target
milestones.detail: Target: recover at least 20% of edible food otherwise disposed for people to eat. The 2014 baseline applies to disposal reduction, not this food recovery target.

jurisdictions: Review collection, food recovery capacity, education, procurement, and enforcement duties.
Ask Solana Center about inspection, training, and reporting support.
businesses: Confirm local organics service and train staff on accepted materials.
If your business is a mandated food donor, arrange recovery agreements and keep required records.
farms: Ask your jurisdiction about compost-use partnerships and local organics rules.
Keep edible food recovery for people separate from animal feed and composting.
residents: Use your local organics collection instructions and prevent food waste.
Learn home composting through Solana Center; check how it fits your local service rules.

sources.title: CalRecycle: food recovery questions and baselines
CalRecycle: local collection options and exceptions

caveat: This covers the organics and food recovery program. Waivers, exemptions, and local service rules apply. Farm participation is site-specific; this is not a claim that every farm must accept food waste or compost. Solana Center support does not transfer a jurisdiction's legal duties.

title: Reduce packaging waste at the source
statusLabel: Rules in effect · plan under review
summary: Packaging producers fund and organize waste prevention and recovery under California's producer responsibility system. Rules are in effect. Circular Action Alliance's first plan is under state review; the law sets binding targets for 2032.
who: CalRecycle oversees the program. Circular Action Alliance is the approved producer responsibility organization. Covered producers fund compliance; jurisdictions and recycling providers have collection duties and exemption routes.
solanaRole: Solana Center explains SB 54 and offers plastic-waste education, business consultations, waste audits, staff training, and support for local governments.

milestones.label: Law enacted
milestones.detail: Governor Newsom signed the Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act.

milestones.label: Permanent rules take effect
milestones.detail: The Office of Administrative Law approved the regulations; they took effect upon filing the same day.

milestones.label: First plan comment deadline
milestones.detail: CalRecycle received Circular Action Alliance's plan on October 13, 2026. Public comments close November 13; receipt does not mean approval.

milestones.label: First source reduction target
milestones.detail: The PRO's statewide target is 10% source reduction, including at least 2% through reuse or refill, against the 2023 baseline.

milestones.label: 2032 packaging requirements
milestones.detail: 100% of covered material must be recyclable or compostable. Plastic covered material must reach a 65% recycling rate and a 25% reduction by weight and by plastic component count against 2023.

jurisdictions: Review covered-material collection requirements with your recycling provider and the PRO.
Use CalRecycle's process for any needed collection extension or exemption.
businesses: Check covered-producer status, exclusions, reporting, and participation requirements with CalRecycle.
Ask Solana Center about reducing single-use materials and training staff.
farms: Check covered-producer status for branded produce packaging.
Review reusable or refillable packaging options that suit your products.
residents: Choose reuse and refill where available.
Follow local sorting rules; a product label alone does not confirm local collection.

sources.title: CalRecycle: SB 54 status and plan review
CalRecycle: final rules and effective date
CalRecycle: local government and service provider guidance

caveat: The reduction targets apply collectively through the PRO plan; each producer does not independently owe a 25% cut. The 65% recycling target applies to plastic covered material, not all packaging. Solana's documented role is education and local waste-reduction support, not PRO administration.

title: Build a system for textile reuse and recovery
summary: California is building producer-funded recovery for covered apparel and textiles. Landbell USA is the approved producer responsibility organization. State rules and the collection plan are still being developed; current Solana Center programs focus on education, reuse, and repair.
who: CalRecycle writes and oversees the rules. Covered producers must join the approved PRO, Landbell USA, which prepares the needs assessment and program plan. CalRecycle reports its approval in March 2026.
solanaRole: Solana Center documents textile education, clothing swaps, mending and upcycling events, and presentations for communities, local governments, and businesses. Its textile page explains SB 707.

milestones.label: Law enacted
milestones.detail: Governor Newsom signed the Responsible Textile Recovery Act of 2024.

milestones.label: Producer join deadline
milestones.detail: Covered producers had to join the approved PRO by this date. This was not the opening date for a statewide collection service.

milestones.label: Next public rules workshop
milestones.detail: CalRecycle scheduled an informal workshop on producer plans, contingency plans, plan termination, and annual reports.

milestones.label: Initial needs assessment due
milestones.detail: The PRO must submit its initial statewide needs assessment to CalRecycle.

milestones.label: Earliest rules effective date
milestones.detail: Regulations may take effect no earlier than this date. It is not a confirmed collection launch date.

jurisdictions: Share local reuse, repair, and collection needs during program development.
Ask Solana Center about textile education or a community event.
businesses: Check whether you are a covered producer and confirm PRO participation duties.
Use repair, reuse, and staff education while the state program develops.
farms: Use repair and reuse options for ordinary clothing and linens.
Check product coverage if your business sells apparel or textile goods.
residents: Repair, swap, or donate suitable textiles through existing services.
Check each service's accepted items; future statewide collection is still being developed.

sources.title: Governor of California: September 28, 2024 signing record
CalRecycle: textile program status and milestones

caveat: This is SB 707 from 2024, not the 2025 open-meetings law with the same number. Solana's education is documented. A formal PRO partnership or future collection-operator role is not established by these sources. Existing local events are separate from the future statewide program.
